From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This article should list *only* official names approved by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") (IAU).[[1]](#cite_note-IAU-USGS-1)

* Mercurian: 414 craters (7.9%)
* Lunar: 1,624 craters (31.1%)
* Martian: 1,092 craters (20.9%)
* Venusian: 900 craters (17.2%)
* Others: 1,198 craters (22.9%)

Distribution of named [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") in the [Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") as of 2017[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_craters_on_Mercury&action=edit)[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[5]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-5)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-6)

This is a list of named [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") on [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (planet)"), the [innermost planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_planets "Inner planets") of the [Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") *(for other features, see [list of geological features on Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_geological_features_on_Mercury "List of geological features on Mercury"))*.[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2) Most Mercurian craters [are named after](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetary_nomenclature "Planetary nomenclature") famous writers, artists and composers. According to the rules by IAU's [Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_Group_for_Planetary_System_Nomenclature "Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature"), all new craters must be named after an artist that was famous for more than fifty years, and dead for more than three years, before the date they are named.[[6]](#cite_note-Ritzel-7) Craters larger than 250 km in diameter are referred to as "basins" *(also see [§ Terminology](#Terminology))*.[[7]](#cite_note-8)[[8]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Categories-9)

As of 2025[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_craters_on_Mercury&action=edit), there are 444 named Mercurian craters,[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2) a small fraction of the total number of named Solar System craters, most of which are [lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon"), [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars") and [Venerian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Venus "List of craters on Venus") craters.[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[5]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-5)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-6)

Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [Callisto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callisto_(moon) "Callisto (moon)") ([141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Callisto "List of craters on Callisto")), [Ganymede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganymede_(moon) "Ganymede (moon)") ([131](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Ganymede "List of craters on Ganymede")), [Rhea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhea_(moon) "Rhea (moon)") (128), [Vesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4_Vesta "4 Vesta") (90), [Ceres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceres_(dwarf_planet) "Ceres (dwarf planet)") (90), [Dione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dione_(moon) "Dione (moon)") (73), [Iapetus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iapetus_(moon) "Iapetus (moon)") (58), [Enceladus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enceladus_(moon) "Enceladus (moon)") (53), [Tethys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tethys_(moon) "Tethys (moon)") (50) and [Europa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_(moon) "Europa (moon)") ([41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Europa "List of craters on Europa")). For a full list, *see [List of craters in the Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_in_the_Solar_System "List of craters in the Solar System")*.

|caption=Distribution of named [[Impact crater|craters]] in the [[Solar System]] {{as of|2017|lc=y}}{{efn|name=WGPSN-Dropped}} }} This is a list of named [[Impact crater|craters]] on [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]], the [[Inner planets|innermost planet]] of the [[Solar System]] ''(for other features, see [[list of geological features on Mercury]])''. Most Mercurian craters [[Planetary nomenclature|are named after]] famous writers, artists and composers. According to the rules by IAU's [[Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature]], all new craters must be named after an artist that was famous for more than fifty years, and dead for more than three years, before the date they are named. Craters larger than 250 km in diameter are referred to as "basins" ''(also see {{Section link||Terminology}})''.[https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/Projects/PlanetaryMapping/DIGGEOL/mercury/h7/h7.pdf H-7 text\_all.word] {{As of|2025}}, there are 444 named Mercurian craters, a small fraction of the total number of named Solar System craters, most of which are [[List of craters on the Moon|lunar]], [[List of craters on Mars|Martian]] and [[List of craters on Venus|Venerian]] craters.{{efn|name=WGPSN-Dropped}} Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [[Callisto (moon)|Callisto]] ([[List of craters on Callisto|141]]), [[Ganymede (moon)|Ganymede]] ([[List of craters on Ganymede|131]]), [[Rhea (moon)|Rhea]] (128), [[4 Vesta|Vesta]] (90), [[Ceres (dwarf planet)|Ceres]] (90), [[Dione (moon)|Dione]] (73), [[Iapetus (moon)|Iapetus]] (58), [[Enceladus (moon)|Enceladus]] (53), [[Tethys (moon)|Tethys]] (50) and [[Europa (moon)|Europa]] ([[List of craters on Europa|41]]). ## Nomenclature News

#### Name Approved for Io: Aganjú Fluctus

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Aganjú Fluctus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16518) for a feature on Io. For more information, please see the [Io nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/io_comp_color.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Mars: Merchant, Ilgenfritz, and Reine

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Merchant](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16515), [Ilgenfritz](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16516), and [Reine](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16517) for three craters on Mars. For more information, please see the [MC-27](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc27_2014.pdf) and [MC-29](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc29_2014.pdf) nomenclature maps in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Mercury: Mangeshkar, Ashevak, Nwapa, Montgomery, Na Hye-sŏk, Noonuccal, and Albizu

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Mangeshkar](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16508), [Ashevak](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16509), [Nwapa](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16510), [Montgomery](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16511), [Na Hye-sŏk](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16512), [Noonuccal](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16513), and [Albizu](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16514) for seven features on Mercury. For more information, please see the [H-4](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-4.pdf), [H-5](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-5.pdf), [H-9](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-9.pdf), [H-10](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-10.pdf), and [H-11](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-11.pdf) nomenclature quad maps in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for a Ring Arc of Neptune: Sincérité

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name Sincérité for a ring arc of Neptune. For more information, please see the [Ring and Ring Gap Nomenclature page](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Page/Rings) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Donaldjohanson: Natunuku Dorsum

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Natunuku Dorsum](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16507) for a feature on Donaldjohanson. For more information, please see the [Donaldjohanson nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/donaldjohanson.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Mercury: Mirabilis Rupes

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Mirabilis Rupes](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16506) for a feature on Mercury. For more information, please see the [H-11 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-11.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for the Moon: McLaughlin D

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [McLaughlin D](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16505) for a feature on the Moon. For more information, please see the [LAC-21 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Lunar/lac_21_wac.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Enceladus: Euphrates Sulcus and Fars Sulcus

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Euphrates Sulcus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16503) and [Fars Sulcus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16504)
for two features on Enceladus. For more information, please see the [Enceladus nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/enceladus_comp.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Mars: Pals

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Pals](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16502) for a feature on Mars. For more information, please see the [MC-4 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc4_2014.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Dione: Hector and Andromache

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Hector](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16500) and [Andromache](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16501) for two features on Dione. For more information, please see the [Dione nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/dione_comp.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Codesido](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16347), [Wu Shujuan](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16348), [El Husseini](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16349), [Freire](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16350), [Asawa](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16351), [Halim](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16352), [Bilokur](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16353), and [Le Guin](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16354) for eight craters on Mercury. For more information, please see the [H-3](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-3.pdf), [H-5](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-5.pdf), [H-7](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-7.pdf), and [H-15](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-15.pdf) nomenclature maps in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).
